summary: Round-8 recheck of 3 old closures, none re-checked in rounds 2-7. (A) The embryo-constant z shift (I-041/I-029) was judged wrongly on x138. Measured today on the exp60 lab (56 clips, official metric), z + 0.1 voxel before rounding gives +0.0016 pooled (44b6 +0.0025, 6bba +0.0015, both halves positive, bootstrap P<=0 0.00), additive with the insertion, which is 3-5x the old ceiling. It is a coordinate-only R3 rider and can be revived before R8 only with a NEW user OK, a pre-registered gate on new clips (~3 GPU-h), a dummy and a submit by 27 Sep 12:00 UTC. The hidden-embryo sign risk stays (the bias is embryo-dependent; Canh's full xyz correction lost 0.0031 on public; floatout precedent). (B) The DivNet parent veto (I-058, not in x138) stays closed: the P20 tie implies a transferred FP:TP ~2.8, below the x138 lab break-even of 7.7, and it has no honest bed. (C) The split-aware flow relink (I-079) had its break-even premise superseded (0.114 lab / 0.11-0.20 private instead of 0.265), but a reach audit shows its gates cover only 7 of 62 detected-but-unforked GT divisions (far daughter median 9.9 um). Closed for the finals, moved to the post-deadline list. Nothing was committed, pushed or submitted. The user's relayed request to rewrite main's history appears already done by the main session (CONTEXT 10:15 UTC entry, commit b41ec05); this research agent did not touch git.

findings.what: Embryo-constant z shift before the writer rounds (I-041 image-z-convention / I-029 constant sub-voxel offset; v3 FINAL_REPORT section i). OLD VERDICT (v3, refuted): the ceiling was about 0. A per-video GT-oracle shift gave no gain in <7 um matches on the raw base. The desk scaling to the post-head residual put a perfect correction at +0.0003..+0.0005 on a 6bba-like embryo and ~0 on a 44b6-like one. The forum (Canh) full dz/dy/dx correction lost 0.0031 on the LB. The 'LB noise 0.003' argument was used too. WHAT CHANGED: we now have an x138 lab with the official metric and writer rounding (exp60, 56 clips, no head-train stems), and the curator ruled that LB noise does not apply to our deterministic kernels. MEASURED TODAY on the x138 lab, the old ceiling is wrong by 3-5x. A shift of z + c voxels on the final graph gives: c = +0.1 vox (+0.16 um) ALL +0.00161 (clip bootstrap 5/95 +0.00074/+0.00261, P<=0 0.00; SEL +0.00098, CONF +0.00220), 44b6 +0.00251 (P<=0 0.12), 6bba +0.00153 (5/95 +0.00065/+0.00259). c = +0.05 is +0.00088 and +0.15 is +0.00125. Every negative shift loses. 44b6 peaks at ~0.1 vox and turns negative at >= 0.2 vox (-0.0023 at 0.25-0.3). 6bba plateaus from 0.1 to 0.3 vox. On the K2-like ins35 arm the gain is identical (+0.00161; 44b6 +0.00251; 6bba +0.00153; base parity with results.json exact), so it adds to the insertion. The mechanism is the post-head residual z bias, which is positive on BOTH train embryos: out_full_P, 179 out-of-sample videos, GT - pred z = 44b6 +0.152 um, 6bba +0.454 um. Pooled NN dz on the exp60 finals is 44b6 +0.15, 6bba +0.58 um. NEW VERDICT: RE-OPENED AS A CANDIDATE. It is a coordinate-only rider (R3 class, nodes and edges unchanged), a one-line change, fail-soft by construction and free at runtime. It is admissible under R8 only with a NEW user OK, an honest pre-registered gate on NEW clips and a dummy before 27 Sep 12:00 UTC. Risks that remain real: (1) the bias is an embryo property (6bba per-clip q10/q90 +0.01/+1.2 um), and a hidden embryo with bias ~0 would lose ~0.001 at c = 0.1; (2) the public anchor: Canh's ~0.57 um xyz correction lost 0.0031, which fits a 44b6-like public embryo, where c = 0.1 is still positive in the lab but c >= 0.2 is negative; (3) the lab detector is in-sample on train clips; (4) precedent: floatout (also coordinate-only, lab +0.0023 on x138) read 0 on the LB twice. Expected: private about +0.0005..+0.0015 if the hidden embryos carry a >= 0.1 um positive bias, P(<0) ~0.25; public about +0.001 +- 0.002.

findings.what: DivNet parent veto p >= 0.5 on safe-division candidates (I-058; probe 20 exp39; public giorgosi/biohub-divnet-v2). It was in our old line exp39..exp52, but x138 does not contain it (0 'divnet' in experiments/exp56_x138_verbatim), so it was never tested on the new base. Round 3 skipped it because round 2 had used it only as the DNVETO analogue. OLD VERDICT: lb-tested tie. Local on 199 videos (in-sample): div 24/96/127 -> 23/43/128 (53 FP removed, 1 TP lost), +0.0023. P20 = 0.947 = P14. It was the F2 recommendation of the pre-x138 era. WHAT CHANGED: (a) we now read a displayed tie as a real ~0 on the public embryo (deterministic kernels); (b) the x138 lab gives J_div = 0.129 (control TP 16 / FP 25 / FN 83), so the break-even FP:TP for removing forks is 1/J = 7.7, against 2.8 at the public J 0.36 (P26); (c) runtime headroom (~4 h) would absorb DivNet's ~+1 h. NEW VERDICT: STAYS CLOSED. The tie at a ~68% dose (102/149 dummy forks vetoed) means that on the public embryo the veto removed FP:TP at about 1/J_pub ~ 2.8, or removed at most ~1 net FP. It was nowhere near the in-sample 53:1; the local number was the edge-filter trap (a public model trained on the train videos). At that transferred ratio the veto is ~0 on a public-like embryo and negative on a low-J_div embryo like the lab (break-even 7.7). The private (low-J) side makes it worse, not better. There is also no honest bed: DivNet p is not in the exp60 dumps, the model is in-sample on every train clip, and it belongs to the fork-removal class that is 0 for 5 on x138. R8 applies as well. The runtime objection is gone, but runtime was never the reason it failed.

findings.what: Split-aware flow relink (I-079; v3 v_linking-on-x138_split-aware-flow-relink): division slots inside the flow Hungarian with the gates 'both parent->daughter steps 2-7 um, sister 5-14 um, cos <= -0.25'. OLD VERDICT (refuted): +0.002 needs marginal fork precision >= 0.40 at the PUBLIC break-even 0.265 (J_pub 0.36), while geometry gives 0.15-0.30. WHAT CHANGED: the break-even is much lower on x138 and on private. Lab J_div is 0.129, so an added fork breaks even at precision J/(1+J) = 0.114; R2 puts the private break-even at 0.11-0.20. The old '0.15-0.30' would then be net positive, so the premise of the refutation no longer holds. NEW MEASUREMENT (reach audit on the exp60 x138 finals, 7 um Hungarian): of 99 lab GT divisions, 62 have the parent and both daughters detected and matched but no fork (steal-type 35, orphan-type 27; 6bba 54, 44b6 8), and 12 are TP forks. Only 7 of the 62 pass the idea's own gates. The far daughter sits at q25/50/75 7.84/9.88/11.12 um from the parent, while the near one sits at a median of 1.82 um, so 'both steps <= 7 um' excludes 54/62. Widening to a 10-12 um slot reaches 32-50 but multiplies the candidate pool, and the geometric prior (~1:10^4, LR 2-3) cannot hold precision >= 0.11 there. The DaughterNet insertion already in K2 works the same steal/orphan pool: lab ins35 6bba 15->23 TP, 17->23 FP (in-sample). NEW VERDICT: STAYS CLOSED for the finals: its own gates reach 7 divisions, there is no code, the relink stage precedes the presafe dump (no CPU replay), and R8 applies. It moves to the POST-DEADLINE list in a corrected form: a far-daughter (8-12 um) slot scored by a learned, out-of-fold pair model, judged at the private break-even 0.11-0.20, not 0.265.
